ambiguities: Local indices are inventory indices unless board uses a clearly numbered product sequence. They are not global design IDs.
After Hours board prints socks twice (23 and24), then boxer briefs also24. It contains25 visual product slots but24 garment/accessory categories if socks are grouped.
Five-family batch boards have construction variants and independent colour/pattern options. This does not prove every construction×colourway combination is approved or equals a discrete SKU.
Art capsule boards contain full-look combinations; do not count those as additional single garments without separating constituent pieces.
Repeated category names across audience,collection,construction,artwork and panel arrangements are related silhouettes, not evidence of identical design.

Board lettering is raster imagery; tiny technical text and some logo/colour names can be inconsistent. Manufacturer specifications and approval status are not established by labels such as production ready.
Materials, dimensions, placements, print separations, Pantone codes, grading, quantities and manufacturing tolerances cannot be recovered reliably from these images alone.
p14-3 Womens Street Art jersey row depicts six garment images although its printed construction list names five; no sixth SKU should be invented.
p15-2 Street Art tee row appears to include a collared utility garment, despite naming five tee constructions; treat illustrations as concept references where labels disagree.
p12-2 bottom styled-look numbering prints06 for Abstract between03 and05; preserve names and use internal sequential IDs.
p14-2 Art Bottom sidebar says pleated short, while pictured garment caption says pleated skort. Inventory uses caption pleated skort.
Some bulk colour labels have been normalized for spelling and casing; exact production colour standards must be supplied independently.

counts.note: These are reference slots, not deduplicated products, SKUs, approved manufacturing combinations or a claim of753 unique designs.
